claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately reflects the stated purpose of subchapter 8 FAM 801.2 regarding the use of IRLs and INs.
The claim accurately captures the definition and essential components of information request letters (IRLs).
The claim correctly conveys the mandatory requirement to fully adjudicate an application prior to suspension to address all issues.
The claim faithfully records that IRLs have been carefully crafted to communicate statutory, regulatory, and other Department requirements clearly and accurately.

The source specifies that 'Passport agencies/centers' must not make unilateral changes without CA/PPT/S/A approval except with management approval in extenuating circumstances. The claim incorrectly assigns this rule and scope to 'Posts', which are governed separately under paragraph (2).
The claim accurately states the requirement that posts must use the cleared language in the IRLs.
The claim correctly reflects posts' authorization to modify cleared IRL language for local logistical requirements and concerns.
The claim accurately captures the note stating that IRLs are not adjudicative guidance.
The claim correctly details the sequence and duty of adjudicating in accordance with 8 FAM prior to selecting the appropriate IRL.
The claim accurately captures the definition of INs as standardized notices informing passport bearers about their passports.
The claim accurately conveys the source's illustrative examples regarding the inclusion of INs.
The claim accurately captures that INs are crafted to communicate information clearly and accurately.
The claim accurately states the prohibition against unilateral changes to INs at passport agencies/centers and the management approval exception.
The source states that INs 'do not require a response from the applicant'. The claim inverts this into an affirmative requirement, asserting that INs require a response.
The claim accurately captures the exemption that INs do not need to be personalized with the applicant's name and address.
The claim correctly represents posts' permission to consult indexes or email when tailoring correspondence.

The requirement to fully adjudicate prior to suspension is faithfully captured by C0002.
The statement regarding the crafting and communication function of IRLs is fully retained in C0003.
C0004 erroneously identifies the actor and governing scope as Posts rather than Passport agencies/centers.
The exception is misapplied to Posts rather than Passport agencies/centers due to erroneous drafting in C0004.
The mandate for posts to use cleared IRL language is fully retained by C0005.
Posts' authority to modify IRL language to suit local logistical requirements is fully captured by C0006.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the rule allowing generators to accumulate non-acute and acute hazardous waste up to specified threshold quantities at or near the point of generation without standard RCRA permitting, provided all conditions for exemption in the rule are met.

The claim correctly reflects that generators may comply with satellite accumulation exemption conditions in this rule instead of central accumulation conditions in rules 3745-52-16(B) or 3745-52-17(A), subject to the exceptions in (A)(7) and (A)(8).

The claim accurately conveys the duty to immediately transfer hazardous waste to a sound container or to a central accumulation area if a satellite container is not in good condition or begins to leak.
The claim correctly states the requirement to use containers made of or lined with materials compatible with the accumulated hazardous waste.
The claim correctly captures the prohibition against placing incompatible wastes or materials in the same container unless 3745-65-17(B) is met.
The claim correctly states the prohibition against placing hazardous waste into an unwashed container that previously held incompatible material unless rule 3745-65-17(B) is complied with.
The claim correctly states the requirement to separate or protect containers holding hazardous waste from incompatible wastes or materials accumulated nearby.

The claim accurately captures the rule that containers holding hazardous waste must remain closed at all times during accumulation, along with the specified exceptions for adding/removing waste and necessary temporary venting.

In the source text, paragraph (A)(5) requires containers to be marked with both (a) 'Hazardous Waste' AND (b) an indication of hazards. Claim C0008 erroneously frames these two requirements as mutually exclusive alternatives ('with either the words... or an indication...').

Paragraph (A)(6) of the source requires action within 'three consecutive calendar days'. Claim C0009 incorrectly states 'thirty consecutive calendar days' in its summary and choice_text, altering the compliance threshold tenfold.
The claim correctly details the duties during the three-day excess period: continued compliance with paragraphs (A)(1) to (A)(5) and marking containers with the date accumulation began.
The claim correctly states the preparedness, prevention, and emergency procedure standards applicable to satellite accumulation areas operated by small quantity generators.
The claim correctly captures the requirement that large quantity generator satellite accumulation areas comply with rules 3745-52-250 to 3745-52-265.
The claim correctly reports the non-regulatory comment directing readers to rule 3745-50-11 for incorporated publication dates.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately and completely represents the conditional exemption permitting satellite accumulation without standard permits.
Claim C0001 fully preserves the option to comply with satellite accumulation exemption conditions instead of central accumulation conditions.
Claim C0002 completely captures the immediate transfer requirements when a satellite container leaks or deteriorates.
Claim C0003 fully captures the container compatibility mandate.
Claim C0004 preserves the prohibition against commingling incompatible wastes/materials in the same container.
Claim C0005 accurately reflects the prohibition on using unwashed containers previously holding incompatible materials.
Claim C0006 fully captures the separation and protection standard for nearby incompatible wastes.
Claim C0007 completely states the general requirement that containers must remain closed at all times during accumulation.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for adding, removing, or consolidating waste.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for temporary venting necessary for equipment operation.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for temporary venting to prevent dangerous situations such as pressure build-up.
Claim C0008 mistakenly treats the requirement to mark containers with 'Hazardous Waste' as an alternative option rather than an mandatory cumulative requirement along with hazard indication.
Claim C0008 presents indicating hazards as an alternative to marking 'Hazardous Waste' instead of requiring both.
Claim C0009 misstates the compliance deadline as thirty consecutive calendar days instead of three consecutive calendar days.
Claim C0009 misstates the deadline to remove excess waste as thirty days rather than three consecutive calendar days.
Claim C0009 incorporates a thirty-day deadline instead of the mandated three-day period.
Claim C0009 erroneously extends the allowable removal window to thirty consecutive calendar days instead of three.
Claim C0010 accurately conveys the ongoing requirements and container date labeling during the three-calendar-day period.
Claim C0011 fully and correctly covers preparedness and emergency procedure rules for small quantity generators.
Claim C0012 accurately conveys large quantity generator emergency procedure requirements for satellite accumulation areas.
Claim C0013 faithfully captures the informational reference to rule 3745-50-11.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 captures paragraph (A)'s authorization permitting a generator to accumulate up to 55 gallons of non-acute hazardous waste and either 1 quart of liquid acute hazardous waste or 1 kg of solid acute hazardous waste in containers at or near the point of generation without a permit, provided all exemption conditions are satisfied.

Claim C0001 correctly reflects the provision in paragraph (A) allowing a generator to comply with the satellite accumulation exemption conditions instead of central accumulation area conditions under rule 3745-52-16(B) or 3745-52-17(A), except as required in paragraphs (A)(7) and (A)(8).

Claim C0002 accurately extracts the mandatory duty in paragraph (A)(1) to immediately transfer waste from a leaking container or one in poor condition to an intact container or to a compliant central accumulation area.
Claim C0003 correctly represents paragraph (A)(2), requiring containers to be compatible with accumulated hazardous waste so containment is not impaired.
Claim C0004 accurately states the prohibition in paragraph (A)(3)(a) against placing incompatible wastes or materials in the same container unless paragraph (B) of rule 3745-65-17 is complied with.

Claim C0005 accurately states paragraph (A)(3)(b), prohibiting the placement of hazardous waste in an unwashed container that previously held incompatible waste or material unless paragraph (B) of rule 3745-65-17 is complied with.
Claim C0006 accurately states paragraph (A)(3)(c), requiring containers of hazardous waste incompatible with nearby materials to be separated or protected by practical means.

Claim C0007 comprehensively captures the requirement in paragraph (A)(4) to keep accumulation containers closed at all times, together with all explicit statutory exceptions: handling waste, equipment operation venting, and pressure/danger venting.
Claim C0008 accurately states both labeling conditions of paragraph (A)(5): marking with 'Hazardous Waste' and indicating hazards.

Claim C0009 faithfully presents the duties and alternatives in paragraphs (A)(6)(a) and (A)(6)(b) when excess waste accumulates, including the 3-consecutive-calendar-day timeline and all permitted destination options.

Claim C0010 correctly extracts paragraph (A)(6)(c), requiring continued compliance with paragraphs (A)(1) to (A)(5) during the 3-day excess accumulation period and marking containers with the date excess accumulation began.
Claim C0011 correctly states the mandate of paragraph (A)(7) requiring SQG satellite accumulation areas to meet preparedness, prevention, and emergency procedures in rule 3745-52-16(B)(8) and (B)(9).

Claim C0012 accurately preserves the mandate of paragraph (A)(8) requiring LQG satellite accumulation areas to meet the preparedness, prevention, and emergency procedures in rules 3745-52-250 to 3745-52-265.
Claim C0013 preserves the non-regulatory comment cross-referencing rule 3745-50-11 for publication dates incorporated by reference.

Claim C0005 covers the prohibition against placing hazardous waste into an unwashed container that previously held incompatible waste.
Claim C0006 covers the requirement to separate or protect containers holding waste incompatible with nearby materials.
Claim C0007 covers the general duty to keep containers closed at all times during accumulation.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for adding, removing, or consolidating waste.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for temporary venting necessary for equipment operation.
Claim C0007 explicitly incorporates the exception for temporary venting to prevent dangerous situations.
Claim C0008 covers the requirement to mark or label the container with the words 'Hazardous Waste'.
Claim C0008 covers the requirement to mark or label the container with an indication of the hazards of the contents.
Claim C0009 covers the compliance option to comply with CAA requirements within 3 consecutive calendar days when satellite accumulation limits are exceeded.
Claim C0009 covers the option to remove excess waste within 3 days to a compliant central accumulation area.
Claim C0009 covers the option to remove excess waste within 3 days to an on-site permitted or permit-by-rule facility.

Claim C0012 covers the requirement for LQG satellite accumulation areas to meet LQG preparedness, prevention, and emergency procedures.
Claim C0013 covers the incorporated by reference comment pointing to rule 3745-50-11.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately conveys the statement of purpose for subchapter 8 FAM 801.2 regarding guidance on IRLs and INs without omissions or distortions.
Claim C0001 defines IRLs as personalized, standardized letters with date and signature blocks requesting applicant actions, documentation, or information, faithfully mirroring F003.
Claim C0002 captures the mandatory requirement to fully adjudicate the application prior to suspending to ensure all issues are addressed.
Claim C0003 faithfully captures the descriptive statement that IRLs are carefully crafted to communicate statutory, regulatory, and other Department requirements clearly and accurately.

Claim C0004 states the prohibition on passport agencies/centers making unilateral changes to IRLs without CA/PPT/S/A approval, as well as the extenuating-circumstances exception with management approval.
Claim C0005 correctly records the affirmative duty on posts to use the cleared language in the IRLs.
Claim C0006 reflects the authorization granted to posts to modify IRL language to suit local logistical requirements and other local concerns.
Claim C0007 captures the factual clarification that IRLs are not adjudicative guidance.
Claim C0008 accurately captures the procedural requirement to adjudicate the application under 8 FAM before selecting the appropriate IRL to address deficiencies.
Claim C0009 defines INs as standardized notices that provide passport bearers with information about their passports.
Claim C0010 accurately reflects illustrative examples of IN use (explaining limited validity and documentation needed for full validity).
Claim C0011 captures the descriptive statement that INs are carefully crafted to communicate passport information clearly and accurately.
Claim C0012 captures the prohibition on unilateral changes to INs at passport agencies/centers without CA/PPT/S/A approval, and the extenuating-circumstances exception with management approval.
Claim C0013 correctly identifies the exemption that INs do not require a response from the applicant.
Claim C0014 correctly identifies the exemption that INs do not need to be personalized with the applicant's name and address.
Claim C0015 conveys the discretionary authority for posts tailoring correspondence to consult the IRL and IN indexes or contact AskPPTAdjudication@state.gov.
